Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Retention matrix & compliance exceptions — Acme coordination

Team — looping everyone in for a quick triage call + decision path on a couple of asks from Acme. Summary: they need (1) a firm retention window for audit logs tied to their SOC2 evidence request, (2) an exception path for a subset of keys they want BYOK for (customer-managed KMS), and (3) SSO evidence and identity federation notes for procurement.

Attached is the latest retention worksheet Acme shared (acme_retention_matrix_v2.xlsx) and their SOC2 evidence list (acme_soc2_evidence_questions.pdf). Key constraints from Acme:
- Audit logs: 3 years preferred but will accept 12 months if we can provide exportable evidence and tamper-evident hashing.
- BYOK: they want a carveout where only certain workspaces use their KMS, with a documented exception flow for on-boarding.
- SSO: they want confirmation of assertion-level logging and where we store identity metadata.

Asks:
1) Marcus/Mina — can Security/Infra outline feasible retention options and what falls under current platform cost/SLA? Prefer 12m (default) vs 36m (premium) tradeoffs.
2) Karthik — product needs to know whether we can expose a self-service exception workflow for BYOK or whether this stays as an engineering-handled exception.
3) Laura — can you coordinate a short procurement note for Acme on what evidence we can provide in 48 hours vs 7 days?

Proposed next steps before Friday EOD: short internal decision (owner + minimal engineering scope) and a 30‑minute sync with Acme next week.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Sr. Product Manager — Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>

Date: 2027-05-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention matrix & compliance exceptions — Acme coordination

Priyom — thanks for the concise summary. A few quick answers from Security's side:

Audit logs:
- Option A (Standard): 12 months of nearline audit logs with immutable write-once storage (WORM) and SHA256 chaining. This is our current platform default and covered by existing infra budgets.
- Option B (Extended): 36 months archived logs stored in a cold tier (0‑7 day retrieval SLA). This requires an extra cost bucket and a limited storage commitment; estimate ~+$6k/month for a mid-sized Acme footprint.
- Exportability: both options support export to customer S3 with integrity proofs; we can sign exports with a timestamped manifest.

BYOK carveout:
- We can support per-workspace Key Access Policy (KAP) knobs, but the control plane currently assumes platform-managed keys. A true BYOK onboarding where the customer's key material never leaves their KMS requires a short engineering project (2–4 sprints for infra work + rollout docs).
- As an intermediate we can provide a manual exception flow: security creates a scoped key alias and we document the operational steps (audit + playbook). That path is lower friction but not self-serve.

SSO evidence:
- We already store assertion-level logs for SAML and OIDC; however, those logs are kept 90 days in hot storage by default. Extending to 12 months is similar to audit logs scope.

Questions for Product: what is the business bar for self-service vs manual exception? If Acme requires self-service BYOK onboarding we need to plan for dev cycles. If they accept manual exception with documented SLAs, that's much faster.

I'll sketch cost numbers and a short decision matrix by EOD. Attaching a one-page summary next.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>, jane.patterson@acme.com
Date: 2027-05-30T15:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention matrix & compliance exceptions — Acme coordination

Thanks Marcus — this clarifies the tradeoffs. From Product POV:

Priority guidance:
- Default: Offer 12-month audit log retention (standard tier) + exportable manifests. Market expectation and keeps costs predictable.
- Premium: Offer 36-month as a paid add-on (clear uplift on committed contract).
- BYOK: Treat self-service BYOK as a product project (Q3 work) — for current sales motions offer a documented manual exception path and a clear SLA for onboarding (target 14 business days).

Action items I own:
- Draft the customer-facing decision matrix (12m default vs 36m premium; BYOK manual vs self-service roadmap) and a short FAQ to put in the Acme follow-up email. Will have first draft by 2027-05-31 10:00 PDT.
- Define minimal telemetry hooks we need to show we met the export/integrity promises (this is where I need one quick input from Marcus: are signed manifests sufficient or does procurement want certificate-level notarization?).

Priyom — if we align on the manual exception path and commit dates for product roadmap, I think Sales can close with Acme on the premium option. Laura — will you confirm procurement deadlines?

Karthik
Director, Product Management — Platform

Quick operational follow-up after reviewing attachments and Marcus' notes.

Engineering notes and timeline: 
- Manual BYOK exception: we can implement playbook + aliasing + scoped audit in 5 business days (docs + runbook + 1 security review). No code changes required. I'll prepare the runbook and a checklist for Acme to sign off.
- Self-service BYOK: requires infra work to split control plane flows for key provisioning (estimate 6–8 weeks, dependent on prioritization).
- Audit log retention: enabling 36 months as a cold archive toggle can be done with a config flag and data lifecycle policy; storage accounting + billing hookup needs a small billing task (1 sprint).

Deliverables and owners: 
- Marcus — finalize the security one-page and signed-manifest spec (EOD today).
- Karthik — customer-facing matrix & FAQ (by 2027-05-31 10:00 PDT).
- Mina — runbook and exception onboarding checklist + example playbook (deliver by 2027-06-07).
- Laura — procurement note on what we can provide in 48 hours vs 7 days (Laura to send to Acme).

I'll attach a draft runbook in drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeRetention and will share access to Acme's security contact after internal review.

If everyone agrees, I'll start the manual exception onboarding template and schedule the Acme 30-minute sync for next Wednesday.

—Mina
